title: A restocking routine that keeps shelves selling
target: How to keep shelves from running dry during a trading day, using the shelf and stock behaviour the game itself defines.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Enough money for the next order

steps.do: Walk the shelves before you open, not after the first complaint.
steps.because: an empty slot is what triggers the game's own refill behaviour (SpawnProductOnEmptyShelf)

steps.do: Carry the stock in yourself and fill the shelf by hand while the shop is small.
steps.because: restocking is part of the shop logic rather than an instant action (ProductRestockLoop)

steps.do: Keep money aside for the next order instead of spending it all on space.
steps.because: products are tracked by their own product id, so an order you cannot afford means an empty shelf (ProductId)

commonMistakes: Restocking only once a shelf is completely empty.
Spending the day's takings on furniture and leaving nothing for stock.
Assuming every product is orderable from the start.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
